claims.text: The initial Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy is eutectic and has a dual-phase lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure.
The initial inter-lamellar spacing is approximately 2 μm.
The initial alloy has a fracture stress of approximately 944 MPa.
The initial alloy has an elongation of approximately 25.6%.
The initial alloy is brittle or has limited ductility because stress concentrates at incoherent FCC/B2 interfaces.
HPHT treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours will topologically transform the lamellar microstructure into a hierarchical pattern.
The HPHT-induced hierarchical microstructure will have coherent FCC/B2 interfaces replacing incoherent lamellar boundaries.
The specified pressure and temperature lie below the thresholds for phase instability or decomposition.
Coherent FCC/B2 interfaces facilitate dislocation transfer between the phases.
The transformed microstructure promotes stacking-fault formation and deformation twinning.
The coherent hierarchical structure produces a more homogeneous strain distribution.
Dislocation transfer and homogeneous strain distribution reduce interfacial stress concentration and arrest interfacial cracking.
HPHT treatment will significantly improve ductility without sacrificing strength.
The treated sample will exhibit elongated cracks rather than the isolated microcracks of the baseline sample.
The GND densities of the FCC and B2 phases will converge at high strain after HPHT treatment.
The as-cast baseline has incoherent lamellar interfaces.
The as-cast baseline exhibits isolated microcracks and divergent GND densities between its phases.
Excessive pressure or temperature may cause phase decomposition or loss of the eutectic structure.

contradictions.description: The query defines the initial alloy as homogenized, whereas the baseline field defines the comparator as as-cast; these are materially different initial processing states.
